outcome: Rate of vaginal delivery within 24 hours
cohort: 210 pregnant women requiring labor induction were enrolled and divided into low-dose and high-dose misoprostol groups.
finding: High-dose intravaginal misoprostol significantly reduced the induction-to-delivery interval and increased the rate of vaginal delivery within 24 hours compared to low-dose, but was associated with a higher incidence of uterine hyperstimulation.
mod_finding: High-dose misoprostol resulted in a higher rate of vaginal delivery within 24 hours compared to low-dose, with no significant difference in cesarean delivery rates between the groups.
